quick_skim.title: Towards Learning Representations of Policies in Two-Player Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
quick_skim.abstract: We investigate the problem of learning useful policy representations (embeddings) in two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games. We make three contributions: First, we introduce methods of creating datasets of policies for a given game. Second, we propose methods to learn policy representations. Third, we introduce downstream tasks to evaluate the effectiveness of such representations.   We evaluate each dataset method, embedding method, and downstream task on Kuhn and Leduc Poker. Although our methods are very basic, we demonstrate that useful behavioral representations are present in the learned embeddings. To our knowledge, this work is among the first to systematically compare self-supervised learning techniques for learning policy representations in games. Our code is available at https://github.com/VitamintK/ssl-project for others to extend.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Proposes methods to learn policy representations in imperfect-information games, demonstrating behavioral embeddings in Kuhn and Leduc Poker, which extends representation learning techniques applicable to AlphaZero variants.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该工作针对不完美信息博弈中策略表示学习的问题，提出了一套包括数据集构建、表示学习和下游任务评估的方法。在Kuhn和Leduc扑克上的实验表明，即使使用简单方法也能学到有行为意义的策略嵌入。这些方法可迁移至AlphaZero架构的变体，为在更广泛的博弈类型中应用AlphaZero提供了表征基础。
